details: `memory.Service` interface with InMemory (keyword) and Vertex AI RAG backends, namespaced per AppName+UserID. LLM accesses via `loadmemorytool`. The framework does not auto-add sessions; you call `AddSessionToMemory` explicitly. Usable, but only Vertex is a real semantic backend out of the box.

First-class `MemoryManager` with `enable_agentic_memory` / `update_memory_on_run` flags. Stores `UserMemory` rows keyed by `user_id` with topics, feedback, timestamps. Auto-extracts facts and auto-injects via `add_memories_to_context`. Strongest fit for cross-session user memory in this benchmark.

No first-party long-term memory abstraction. Provides `VectorStore` trait (in-memory + Qdrant), embeddings, and a `MemoryProvider` slot, but no pre-built cross-session memory. You assemble it yourself.

Partial via on-disk `CLAUDE.md` files loaded by `setting_sources`; `AgentDefinition.memory: 'user'|'project'|'local'` scopes which file a sub-agent sees. No vector store, embeddings, or semantic recall — purely filesystem-shaped.

First-party `agent-memory/<agentType>/` directory recall with selector + LLM-synthesized modes via `SDKMemoryRecallMessage`. User/project/local scopes from `AgentDefinition.memory`. Still file-based, no vector index — semantic retrieval is BYO MCP.

Sophisticated `unified_memory.Memory` with LanceDB/Qdrant backends, automatic fact extraction, hierarchical scope, consolidation, recency/semantic/importance weighting, and adaptive LLM-driven recall flow. Directly fits the benchmark use case for cross-session memory.

No `Memory` type, no `MemoryStore`, no auto-recall. Cross-session memory must be assembled from `components/retriever` plus a custom middleware that injects retrieved snippets — meaningful effort around the framework.
Genkit does not ship a memory abstraction. The closest substitutes are sessions (state, not vector) and retrievers (RAG at query time). You encode any cross-session memory as documents yourself.

`BaseStore` (namespaced KV + optional vector search) is the long-term memory primitive. Postgres+pgvector and in-memory backends ship; tools call `runtime.store.put/search`. Strong, with the minor gap that there is no auto-extract/auto-recall flow built on top.

First-class `Memory.memory_blocks` with `StaticMemoryBlock`, `VectorMemoryBlock`, and `FactExtractionMemoryBlock`. Blocks are processed in priority order and ejected short-term messages are pushed into vector blocks automatically. Directly fits the benchmark.

`@mastra/memory` ships conversation history, working memory (LLM-summarized), semantic recall (vector-backed), and observational memory across threads. Vector store adapters for Pinecone, Qdrant, Chroma, Astra, Lance, Elasticsearch. First-class fit.

Mem0 adapter (`agent-framework-mem0`, `Mem0Provider.cs`) is the main first-party path, with an experimental in-tree `MemoryFileStore`/`MemoryStore` in `_harness/_memory.py`. Plus Azure AI Search and .NET `TextSearchProvider`. Usable but distributed across adapters; main path is Mem0.

Not built-in. The 10 Session backends store turn-level history only. No vector-search long-term memory primitive ships. For RAG/memory you must wire `FileSearchTool` (OpenAI Vector Stores) or a custom `@function_tool`.

No built-in cross-session semantic memory. The only memory surfaces are `Session` (in-conversation) and the sandbox-only filesystem `memory()` capability (scratchpad inside one sandbox run). Cross-session is BYO.

Built-in `MemoryTool` exists but is Anthropic-native with no in-tree local fallback. For provider-agnostic memory you reach for third-party `pydantic-ai-memory`/`pydantic-ai-backend` packages — partial primitive.

ConversationMemory is in-conversation only. Cross-conversation recall is the combination of `dynamic_context(num_samples, vector_store_index)` plus a `VectorStoreIndexDyn` adapter (12+ companion crates). Partial primitive — you wire the memory layer yourself.

Not in SDK core. `strands-agents-tools` ships `mem0_memory`, `agent_core_memory`, `elasticsearch_memory`, `mongodb_memory` as tools the LLM calls explicitly. Production use is mostly host-built around these tools.

No vector store integration, no embeddings primitive, no memories/facts object. Cross-session continuity is only via re-hydrating from a `SessionManager` snapshot. Long-term semantic memory is fully BYO.
No `Memory` class, no semantic-recall primitive, no concept of cross-session memory in the SDK. Reference report explicitly contrasts this with Mastra/LangGraph. BYO via a vector DB.

Vertex AI RAG via `memory/vertexai/` and the `loadmemorytool` are the only built-in retrieval primitives. No first-party Pinecone/Weaviate/Qdrant/pgvector adapter, no chunkers, no rerankers. You build the rest.

First-class `Knowledge` class with Chroma, Qdrant, Pinecone, Weaviate, Milvus, Mongo Atlas, Lance, PgVector, Singlestore, Cassandra, ClickHouse; many embedders and readers; agentic filters; automatic `search_knowledge` tool. Directly fits the benchmark.

Library-level: `document.rs`, `readers/` (PDF etc.), `embeddings/`, `vector_store/` plus Qdrant integration. Examples like `rag_qdrant_agent` show the pattern. You assemble retrieval; the framework provides building blocks.
No first-party RAG. You layer it as an MCP server or SDK tool. No chunkers, vector stores, embedders, or citation primitives ship.
No built-in vector store, no chunker, no retriever, no citation primitive. BYO via MCP server.

`crewai.knowledge.Knowledge` ships 8+ source types (string/text/CSV/JSON/PDF/Excel/Docx/Docling/custom), automatic chunking + embedding, ChromaDB default + Qdrant, multi-embedder support. Wired at agent/crew level. First-class RAG fit.

First-class `Retriever`, `Indexer`, `Embedder`, `Loader`/`Parser`/`Transformer` interfaces and `eino-ext` adapters for Qdrant, Milvus v1/v2, Redis, OpenSearch v2/v3, Elasticsearch v7-v9, Volc VikingDB, Dify. Strong; minor gap is no out-of-the-box citation primitive.

Strong first-party. `ai.Retriever` action type with built-in plugins (localvec, pinecone, weaviate, postgres+pgvector, alloydb, firebase), chunkers, embedders per provider, and a `Reranker` abstraction. `WithDocs(...)` inlines retrieved docs. Minor gap: no citation rendering primitive.
No native retriever; relies on separately-packaged `langchain-*` vector stores. `BaseStore.search()` covers basic semantic recall but no chunkers, no citation, no reranking ship in this repo.

RAG is LlamaIndex's historical core. 60+ vector store integrations, multiple index types (Vector, Summary, Tree, KnowledgeGraph, PropertyGraph), retrievers (Base/Router/Fusion), built-in citation via CitableBlock/CitationBlock. Best fit in the benchmark.
`@mastra/rag` ships retrievers, chunkers (e.g. recursiveChunker), citation support, integrated with the memory vector adapters. First-class.

`.NET TextSearchProvider` plus `Microsoft.Extensions.AI.Vector` `IVectorStore` are the generic primitives; Azure AI Search adapter is first-party. Usable, but most stores beyond Azure require BYO or community adapters and no built-in citation.
Hosted only: `FileSearchTool` over OpenAI Vector Stores. For non-OpenAI RAG you write `@function_tool` wrappers. Partial primitive — production use is mostly host-built.
`fileSearchTool` (OpenAI hosted file search over vector stores) is the closest built-in. Otherwise BYO retriever as a function tool. No chunkers/citations in-tree.
Embeddings package with OpenAI/Cohere/Google/Bedrock/sentence-transformers/voyage providers, plus a `docs/examples/rag.md`. Vector stores are BYO. Partial primitive.

First-class: `VectorStoreIndex`/`VectorStoreIndexDyn` traits with 12+ companion crates (mongodb, lancedb, qdrant, sqlite, surrealdb, milvus, scylladb, postgres, s3vectors, neo4j, etc.), `EmbeddingsBuilder`, and `agent.dynamic_context(n, store)` to auto-inline retrieved docs. Strong; gap: no in-tree chunkers/citations.
Via `strands-agents-tools/retrieve.py` (Bedrock Knowledge Base) and memory tools. No first-party chunker / embedder primitives in the SDK core. Partial primitive.

Not provided as a first-class subsystem. The `ContextOffloaderPlugin` (offloads tool results to disk/blob with a `retrieve_offloaded_content` tool) is the closest built-in retrieval pattern. Build a vector-search tool yourself.
Ships `embed`, `embedMany`, `cosineSimilarity`, and `rerank`, but no vector store, chunker, retriever, or citation rendering. Use `@ai-sdk/langchain` / `@ai-sdk/llamaindex` for higher-level RAG.

`SearchRequest.AppName` + `SearchRequest.UserID` give per-user scoping naturally. Tenant scoping is by using `AppName` as the tenant key — pays the cost of fully-isolated memory across apps. Usable, with the gap that there is no separate tenant axis.
`UserMemory.user_id` is the scoping key. Per-tenant means prefixing user IDs (`acme:alice`) or filtering at query time on `metadata`. Usable, but no separate tenant dimension.
Not provided — BYO. You namespace your vector-store collections per tenant. The framework offers no tenancy primitive.
Filesystem-shaped — per-tenant `CLAUDE.md` lives under `tenants/<tid>/` and the SDK loads it via `cwd`. Works but is purely directory-based with no enforcement of tenant boundaries.

Not natural: memory dirs are global-per-machine (`~/.claude/agent-memory/`) or project-scoped under `cwd`. To scope per-tenant you set `cwd: /tenants/${tenantId}`. For true cross-tenant served memory, BYO MCP.

`Memory(root_scope='/tenant/acme')` is the natural fit and prefixes all `remember`/`recall` paths. But the framework does not automatically scope by tenant — you instantiate one `Memory` per tenant manually. Usable, with the gap that there is no runtime `with_tenant` filter.

Retriever `Retrieve(ctx, query, opts...)` receives ctx so you pass tenant scope through; the adapter's `Options.SubIndexes` or query filter respects it. Framework does not enforce — your adapter does. Small primitive only.
Not automatic. Retrievers accept a free-form `Options` (e.g. Pinecone namespace, Postgres WHERE) you encode tenant filters into. No Mastra-style automatic namespacing.

Convention via `BaseStore` namespace tuples like `(tenant_id, 'memories')`. Tightened by `@auth.on.store` at the HTTP layer which injects the tenant prefix server-side so external callers cannot escape it. Strong, with the minor gap that enforcement on raw OSS runtime is still BYO.

`Memory.session_id` is the only first-class scoping key. Per-tenant separation requires encoding `tenant:user:session` into `session_id` or using a per-tenant `SQLAlchemyChatStore` (separate DB/schema). Partial primitive.

Memory scoped per `resourceId` in the `memory: { thread, resource }` tuple. `MASTRA_RESOURCE_ID_KEY` is server-controlled so a client cannot read another tenant's memory. Cross-tenant vector separation via index prefixes. First-class fit.

Memory adapters expose `Scope` options (e.g. `Mem0ProviderScope` — `User`, `Session`, `Global`). Tenancy = scope-by-user with tenant ID encoded into the user. Partial primitive — no deeper tenant dimension.
BYO — namespace your vector indexes by tenant_id. No first-party tenancy primitive in the SDK.
Not provided. You namespace yourself by per-tenant `vectorStoreIds` passed to `fileSearchTool`, or by partitioning a custom `Session` implementation. Small primitive only.
Per-tenant scoping is your responsibility — namespace by `tenant_id` in your vector index. No framework primitive.
Not first-class. You scope vector-store collections per tenant yourself (namespace by `tenant_id` in Postgres/Qdrant schema). No framework support.
BYO. The memory tools accept user/agent IDs but tenancy must be encoded in those IDs. Small primitive only.
BYO. Namespace your vector store / DB / S3 prefix by `tenantId` from `invocationState`. No framework support.
BYO — namespace yourself in your vector DB. No first-party tenancy primitive.
